texts.preamble: Satish Chandra vs Union Of India & Ors on 22 May, 2023 Author: Satish Chandra Sharma Bench: Chief Justice, Subramonium Prasad $~18. * In The High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi + W.P.(C) 7260/2015 Satish Chandra Th ve Union Of India & Ors Th Coram: Hon'Ble The Chief Justice Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Subramonium Prasad % 22.05.2023 1. The present writ petition has been filed with the following prayers: "(a) Direct respondents to formulate and implement anti- counterfeit, tamper-evident, hologram with trackable barcode on: (i) lid of water and medicine bottles (ii) flipside of medicine strips, for checking the menace of sale of counterfeit bottled water and medicines, which is adversely impinging fundamental right to health and clean water of Indian citizens.
texts.facts: The present writ petition has been filed with the following prayers: "(a) Direct respondents to formulate and implement anti- counterfeit, tamper-evident, hologram with trackable barcode on: (i) lid of water and medicine bottles (ii) flipside of medicine strips, for checking the menace of sale of counterfeit bottled water and medicines, which is adversely impinging fundamental right to health and clean water of Indian citizens. (b) Direct Respondent authorities to mandatorily enforce Regulation 5(15) of the Bureau of Indian Standards (Certification) Regulations, 1988. The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
texts.arguments: (g) Direct Respondent authorities to coordinate better and act for stringent enforcement of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986, the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Drugs and Cosmetic Act, 1940 and the Rules thereunder, by taking strict action against illegal production of spurious drugs and counterfeit bottled water in order to safeguard fundamental right to health and clean water. (h) pass such order or further order/s as this Hon'ble Court deem fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case in the interest of justice." 2. He also states that the issue of compliance of Notification dated 20th June, 2006 should be dealt with by respondent no.2. 2. However, learned counsel for respondent no.2 states that the issue of hologram in respect of packaged drinking water and mineral water is an issue pertaining to packaging, which has to be dealt with by FSSAI.
texts.petitioner_arguments: He also states that the issue of compliance of Notification dated 20th June, 2006 should be dealt with by respondent no.2. 2.
